key_insight: AlphaFISH combines spatial host and microbiome profiling with AI to map how bacteria and cells interact in colorectal tumors and to predict recurrence risk after surgery.
clinical_relevance: The approach could help identify high-risk colorectal cancer patients from biopsy tissue and support more precise post-resection monitoring.
method: Sequencing-free spatial profiling at subcellular resolution on 149 colorectal biopsies from 68 patients
Integrated spatial transcriptomics, spatial microbiome data, and a 4.27-million-cell scRNA-seq atlas for annotation
Trained a transformer model on >10 million subcellular sampling vectors to jointly model gene expression, tissue architecture, and microbes
evidence_signal: The model reached nearly 90% accuracy for pathological feature prediction on unseen spatial omics inputs and 81% accuracy for 1-year recurrence prediction in 28 followed patients.
watch_item: This is a promising cohort-scale study, but recurrence performance was tested in a relatively small follow-up group and will need broader external validation before clinical use.
paper_title: Cohort-scale Spatial Host-Microbiome Predicts Post-Resection Recurrence in Colorectal Cancer
